records.exception_reason: Foundational source for tiered-memory and context-compaction mechanics.

claim_snippets.claim_text: MemGPT manages a 'main context' (fixed window) by moving older or irrelevant segments to a larger 'archival memory'backing store via a tiered-storage model.
The agent identifies the need for compaction when the current turn's token usage exceeds 80% of the maximum allowed; it then uses a 'yield' token to trigger a summarization turn.

records.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
records.relevance_note: A primary architectural guide for how to handle long-running agent contexts with caching and compaction.
records.reason_included: Explicit recommendation for using 'milestone summaries' instead of continuous rolling summaries to preserve planning state.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Milestone summaries occur at task boundaries (e.g., after successful verification) and are more resilient to 'telephone game' distortion than rolling summaries.
Prompts should be structured to keep fixed state (rules, tools) at the start and dynamic state (history) at the end to maximize cache-hit rates during incremental execution.

records.title: AriadneMem: Threading the Maze of Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents
records.relevance_note: A state-of-the-art paper on validating summaries during context compaction.
records.reason_included: Mechanism for 'summary-validation turns' to prevent cumulative error in long-horizon agent state.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Before finalizing a compaction, the agent must perform a 're-anchor test' where it attempts to reproduce the most recent task state using only the proposed summary.
Threaded summaries preserve dependency chains (e.g., File A depends on File B) as metadata outside the NL summary to prevent 'blind edits' after compaction.

records.title: Compaction
records.exception_reason: Published after the March 24, 2026 primary-window cutoff; retained for the explicit compaction trigger, emitted handoff item, and pruning behavior in the OpenAI API compaction guide.
records.relevance_note: Compaction is a official doc source with details on server side compaction, standalone compaction relevant to context engineering.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on context, cost budget, state.

claim_snippets.claim_text: OpenAI documents two compaction modes for long-running interactions: server-side threshold-triggered compaction and a standalone compact endpoint for explicit control. ([OpenAI Developers][1])

With server-side compaction enabled, crossing the configured threshold causes the server to compact in-stream, emit an encrypted compaction item, and prune context before continuing inference. ([OpenAI Developers][1])

The standalone endpoint is stateless: the caller sends the full current window and receives a new compacted window that becomes the canonical next context for the next `/responses` call. ([OpenAI Developers][1])

records.title: Dynamic context discovery
records.relevance_note: Concrete operational patterns for preserving recoverability through compaction.
records.reason_included: Shows what stays raw versus summarized, and how the agent can recover detail after summary loss. ([Cursor][2])

claim_snippets.claim_text: Cursor writes long shell or MCP outputs to files instead of truncating them in-message, then lets the agent inspect them with `tail` and follow-up reads; Cursor says this led to fewer unnecessary summarizations near context limits. ([Cursor][2])
When the context window fills, Cursor triggers summarization to reset the agent into a fresh window, but explicitly notes that knowledge can degrade because the summary is lossy. ([Cursor][2])
After automatic or manual summarization, Cursor gives the agent a reference to the chat history file so it can search for details missing from the summary and recover them on demand. ([Cursor][2])

claim_snippets.claim_text: Claude Code states that as context fills, it compacts automatically and that instructions from early conversation can be lost, so persistent rules should live in `CLAUDE.md`. ([Claude][3])

Its documented order of compaction is to clear older tool outputs first, then summarize the conversation if needed; requests and key code snippets are preserved while detailed early instructions may be lost. ([Claude][3])
Claude Code provides a `Compact Instructions` section in `CLAUDE.md` or a focused `/compact` command to influence what is preserved during compaction. ([Claude][3])

records.title: Automate workflows with hooks
records.relevance_note: Concrete repair pattern for compaction loss using a deterministic reinjection hook.
records.reason_included: Directly documents a mechanism for repairing summary omissions after every compaction. ([Claude][4])

claim_snippets.claim_text: Anthropic states that when Claude’s context window fills, compaction summarizes the conversation to free space and can lose important details. ([Claude][4])
The documented recovery pattern is a `SessionStart` hook with a `compact` matcher that re-injects critical project context after every compaction. ([Claude][4])
Any text the hook command writes to stdout is added to Claude’s context, making reinjection an explicit programmable handoff channel. ([Claude][4])

records.title: Coding Agents are Effective Long-Context Processors
records.relevance_note: Confirms that externalizing state into the filesystem is more effective than relying on long context windows.
records.reason_included: Direct evidence for filesystem-led context management.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Long-context processing can be externalized from latent attention into explicit, executable interactions by allowing agents to organize text in file systems.
Coding agents outperform published SOTA by 17.3% on average when using native tool proficiency rather than passive semantic queries.
